decoys.summary: Lua::replace_registry_value accepts a RegistryKey from another independent Lua state and uses its numeric ID in the receiving state. When the two states have live keys with the same ID, replacing the foreign key silently overwrites the unrelated local registry value instead of rejecting the key.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify cross-state RegistryKey acceptance specifically in Lua::replace_registry_value and the resulting overwrite of a colliding local registry slot. A report about foreign Table or Function handles alone does not match.

refutation.evidence: The ownership check at src/state.rs:1895-1897 runs before value conversion or registry access and returns Error::MismatchedRegistryKey. RawLua::owns_registry_value compares the identity of the per-state registry unref-list Arc, not numeric IDs (src/state/raw.rs:334-336). The executed test decoy_1_foreign_registry_replace_is_rejected allocated ID 5 in each of two independent Lua states, attempted the claimed replacement, received MismatchedRegistryKey, and confirmed both original values and the foreign key ID were unchanged. See evidence/control_probes.rs:6 and evidence/probe-run.log.

decoys.summary: With default Serde deserialization options, LuaSerdeExt::from_value rejects an acyclic table that contains the same child table under two sibling keys. The visited-pointer set retains the child after the first branch, so the second branch fails with recursive table detected even though there is no cycle.
decoys.match_rule: The report must identify false cycle detection during Lua-to-Rust Serde deserialization of repeated references to the same child table in separate sibling branches of an acyclic graph. Unbounded nesting depth or rejection of an actual cycle does not match.

refutation.evidence: RecursionGuard is scoped to each table traversal (src/serde/de.rs:303 and 351). Its Drop implementation removes that table pointer at src/serde/de.rs:732, so visited contains the active traversal path, not every previously encountered table. Test decoy_2_shared_acyclic_tables_deserialize first confirmed that left and right are handles to the very same Lua table, then successfully deserialized both branches into serde_json::Value using defaults. It also deserialized a sequence containing the same child twice into Vec<Vec<i64>> and verified both full children. As a distinguishing check, an actual self-cycle returned recursive table detected. See evidence/control_probes.rs:25 and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Chunk::eval retries a failing expression as a statement and duplicates side effects
false_findings.body: Chunk::eval falls back to executing the original source as a statement when expression evaluation returns an error. A call expression such as bump_then_fail(), whose function increments a counter and then raises a Lua error, is valid in both forms. Evaluating it therefore invokes the function twice before returning the error, duplicating mutations made before the failure. The fallback should be limited to expression compilation failures.

refutation.evidence: The if-let at src/chunk.rs:596 tests only self.to_expression(), which loads a Function without executing it (src/chunk.rs:724-744). Once that succeeds, the result of function.call(()) at line 597 is returned directly, including any runtime error; the statement branch is not reached. Test false_1_eval_runtime_error_does_not_retry evaluated bump_then_fail(), observed the original RuntimeError and counter == 1, and separately confirmed that a statement-only increment took the compilation fallback and executed exactly once. See evidence/control_probes.rs:44 and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Chaining Function::bind reverses the order of bound argument groups
false_findings.body: Each Function::bind wrapper prepends its captured arguments before forwarding to the previous wrapper, so the most recently bound group reaches the underlying function first. Binding ("first", nil), then binding "second", and finally calling with "call" delivers ("second", "first", nil, "call") rather than ("first", nil, "second", "call"). Code that binds positional configuration in multiple steps consequently calls Lua functions with parameters in the wrong positions.

refutation.evidence: args_wrapper_impl appends captured arguments and rotates them ahead of the current call arguments (src/function.rs:203-215). The Lua wrapper then calls the previously bound function, whose own wrapper prepends its older group ahead of that entire argument list (src/function.rs:249-252). Thus older bindings remain first. Test false_2_chained_bind_keeps_argument_order_and_nil exercised the exact two groups and call argument, checked argc == 4 and the complete tuple (first, nil, second, call), and verified the original bound function retained its own arguments. See evidence/control_probes.rs:63 and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Function::set_environment changes sibling closures through their shared _ENV
false_findings.body: On Lua 5.4, closures created in the same lexical scope can share one _ENV upvalue. Function::set_environment replaces the value in that shared upvalue, so changing one closure to use a restricted environment also redirects its sibling closures to that table. A sibling that should still read marker from its original environment instead reads marker from the newly supplied environment, violating per-function environment isolation.

refutation.evidence: For Lua 5.2/5.3/5.4, set_environment compiles a fresh return _ENV function using the new table (src/function.rs:325-331), then lua_upvaluejoin at line 333 redirects only the target closure upvalue to that fresh upvalue cell. It does not assign a new value into the existing shared cell. Test false_3_environment_change_isolates_sibling_closures proved initial cell sharing by reassigning the captured lexical _ENV and seeing both closures change. After f.set_environment(new), f read the new marker while its sibling retained the shared environment. Replacing the old cell again changed only the sibling; mutating the new table changed only f. See evidence/control_probes.rs:77 and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Reentering a mutable Rust callback panics instead of returning a Lua error
false_findings.body: Lua::create_function_mut stores its FnMut closure in a RefCell and keeps the mutable borrow while user code runs. If that callback looks up and invokes its own Lua function before returning, the wrapper attempts another mutable borrow and raises a Rust RefCell panic instead of returning an mlua error. Ordinary safe callback recursion can therefore unwind out of Function::call and bypass Result-based error handling.

refutation.evidence: The wrapper uses try_borrow_mut, not borrow_mut, and maps borrow failure to Error::RecursiveMutCallback before invoking the closure (src/state.rs:1290). Test false_4_recursive_mut_callback_returns_error_without_panic reentered the same registered function through globals. catch_unwind returned normally with an Err whose CallbackError cause chain contained RecursiveMutCallback; an invocation counter proved the inner FnMut body never ran. A subsequent nonrecursive call succeeded, proving the borrow was released after the error. See evidence/control_probes.rs:120 and evidence/probe-run.log.

false_findings.title: Lua integer conversion silently wraps out-of-range Rust byte values
false_findings.body: The integer FromLua conversion fast path treats successful lua_tointegerx conversion as sufficient and narrows the resulting Lua integer to the destination Rust integer without checking that type's range. Reading -1 or 256 as u8 therefore succeeds with 255 or 0, and reading 128 as i8 succeeds with -128. Lua-provided integer configuration can consequently be silently corrupted instead of producing FromLuaConversionError.

refutation.evidence: The cast function is num_traits::cast, imported at src/conversion.rs:11, and returns Option after checking representability. Both the Value path (lines 831 and 850-854) and the stack fast path (lines 864-868) convert None into FromLuaConversionError with out of range. The macro is instantiated for i8 and u8 at lines 878-879. Test false_5_narrow_integer_conversions_reject_overflow checked u8(-1), u8(256), and i8(128) through both FromLua::from_lua(Value::Integer) and Chunk::eval, and all six conversions returned the range error. Exact valid endpoints u8(0/255) and i8(-128/127) succeeded. See evidence/control_probes.rs:147 and evidence/probe-run.log.
